key_insight: KANs can accurately predict airfoil surface pressure and interpolate across Mach number and angle of attack, but they do not clearly outperform well-tuned MLPs and are slightly below the best GNN results.
engineering_relevance: For aerodynamic surrogate modeling, KANs offer a potentially faster, lower-complexity alternative for pressure prediction, though model selection must balance accuracy, training stability, and tuning effort.
method: Compare KAN, MLP, and GNN surrogate models for airfoil pressure prediction.
Train on subsonic and transonic airfoil cases to predict full surface pressure coefficient distributions.
Evaluate interpolation across Mach number and angle of attack.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that KANs perform well on full pressure coefficient prediction and interpolation, but are marginally inferior to a suitably trained MLP, while a GNN achieves the best accuracy at the cost of longer training.
watch_item: KAN performance is highly sensitive to hyperparameter optimization and can suffer from training instabilities.
paper_title: Kolmogorov Arnold networks (KAN) for aerodynamic prediction: a comparison with MLPs and GNNs
